title: DSA - Bucket Sort
description:
## Bucket Sort
Bucket sort works differently from comparison sorts. Instead of comparing elements, it distributes them into "buckets" based on their value, sorts each bucket, then concatenates.

### How it works:
1. Create empty buckets (one per range of values)
2. Put each element into its bucket
3. Sort each bucket (using any sort - insertion sort works well)
4. Concatenate all buckets

### Visualization:
```
Input: [23, 1, 45, 12, 37, 8, 31]
Buckets (range 0-9, 10-19, 20-29, 30-39, 40-49):
  [0-9]:   [1, 8]
  [10-19]: [12]
  [20-29]: [23]
  [30-39]: [37, 31] -> [31, 37]
  [40-49]: [45]
Result: [1, 8, 12, 23, 31, 37, 45]
```

**Big O: O(n + k)** average where k is the number of buckets. **O(n²)** worst case if everything lands in one bucket.

Bucket sort is great when input is uniformly distributed across a known range.

---
## Assignment:
Implement `bucket_sort` that sorts positive integers. Use 10 buckets based on value ranges. Assume max value is less than 100.

### Steps:
- [ ] Create 10 empty bucket vectors (bucket 0 = values 0-9, bucket 1 = 10-19, etc.)
- [ ] Put each element into its bucket (`arr[i] / 10`)
- [ ] Sort each bucket (use your insertion sort)
- [ ] Concatenate all buckets back into arr
